READ FIRST, in this order — this is the binding contract:
1. `docs/design-system.md` — tokens, components, and an AUDITED table of what does NOT exist. Read the whole thing before you design anything.
2. `app/globals.css` — the "KODELY PRODUCT SURFACE" and "PRODUCT UTILITIES" blocks.
3. `components/ui/*` — the primitives. Import them; never hand-roll a second version.
4. `components/app/AppShell.tsx`, `components/app/nav.ts`, `app/(portal)/layout.tsx` — the shell. Your pages render CONTENT ONLY: no nav, no page background, no second ToastProvider.

HARD RULES:
- **Never build something that only pretends to work.** If data does not exist, say so on the page with `EmptyState kind="unavailable"` and report it. The "What does not exist" table is authoritative.
- No new npm dependencies. Server Components by default; `"use client"` only where interaction needs it.
- `k-focus` on every interactive element. `k-num` on every figure. `k-scroll-x` on any wide block.
- Harden every search/query param with `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call` — never `x in OBJ`.
- Must pass `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint` on your paths with ZERO errors and ZERO warnings. Run both yourself and fix everything.
- Other agents are working in parallel. **Only touch the files you own.**

YOU OWN: `app/(portal)/dashboard/page.tsx`, `app/(portal)/dashboard/ProjectRow.tsx`, `app/(portal)/dashboard/NewProjectButton.tsx`, `app/(portal)/dashboard/SignOutButton.tsx`, `app/(portal)/dashboard/TopUpButton.tsx`, everything under `app/(portal)/dashboard/websites/`, and `components/app/WebsiteCard.tsx` (new). Do NOT touch `app/(portal)/dashboard/billing/**` or `app/(portal)/dashboard/usage/**` (another agent owns those), or anything in `app/projects/`.

## TASK 1 — Home dashboard (`/dashboard`)

It must answer, in this order: what have I built, what do I do next, how am I doing on credits, does anything need attention.

- **Welcome + primary CTA.** "Welcome back, <name>" and one primary button, "Create Website" → `/dashboard/new`. Exactly one `primary` button on the page. A `k-wash` hero panel is appropriate here — one per page maximum.
- **Websites overview** — the customer's most recent sites as cards, with a "View all" to `/dashboard/websites`.
- **Usage summary** — credits remaining, and `averageBuildCredits()` translated into "about N more builds". Read `lib/credits.ts` for what is genuinely available. There is NO reset date and NO monthly allowance; do not imply one.
- **Recent activity.** `Event` is per-user indexed (`@@index([userId, createdAt])`) and already queried this way in `app/admin/users/[id]/page.tsx`. Roughly `project.created`, `build.succeeded`, `build.failed`, `project.published`, `project.deleted` are the meaningful ones. **Warning from the audit:** `Event.props` carries `projectId` but NOT the project name, so rendering "Published Acme Cafe" needs a join, and a deleted project has no name to join to. Handle that honestly rather than printing a raw id.
- **Quick actions** — only for things that are real.
- Keep `components/onboarding/FirstRunChecklist.tsx` working; restyle its placement if useful but do not break it.

## TASK 2 — My Websites (`/dashboard/websites`)

The most important management page in the portal.

- Grid view AND list view (use `Segmented`), search, sort, and filters.
- **Filters: be honest.** The audit found there is no `status` column — only `publishedAt` gives Published vs Draft, and **"Archived" is not representable at all** (no soft-delete column; `app/api/projects/[id]/route.ts:190` says so outright). "Building" is derivable from `Build.status = "RUNNING"` but there is no cleanup for abandoned SSE requests, so a crashed build reads as building forever. **Decide what to offer and justify it** — do not ship an Archived filter that can never match, and if you offer Building, you must add a staleness rule and say what it is.
- Card contents: name, URL, published/draft, last updated, created. Per-card actions via `Menu`: Open, Edit, Rename, Duplicate, Publish, Delete — all of these are REAL, see `app/api/projects/[id]/route.ts` and `.../publish/route.ts`. Archive is not real: either omit it or use `Menu`'s `unavailableReason`.
- **Thumbnails: nothing captures a screenshot** — no field, no headless browser. Do not render a broken image or a fake screenshot. Design a real solution: my suggestion is a deterministic cover derived from the project's own identity (see `lib/brand-kit.ts` — if a brand kit exists the site's real palette is available; otherwise derive from the slug), clearly reading as a generated cover rather than posing as a screenshot. Use your judgement, but whatever you choose must not lie. Report what you chose.
- Delete must use `ConfirmModal` and must tell the truth about consequences — it is a hard delete and it takes the live site offline.
- The current `NewProjectButton` uses `window.prompt()`. Replace that.

Make both pages fully responsive: sidebar+content on desktop, single column on mobile with the fixed bottom bar already provided by the shell (content already has bottom padding for it).

REPORT BACK concisely: what you built, what you found that was not real, what you deliberately did not build and why, your thumbnail decision, and anything untested — say untested rather than overstating.

1	# Kodely product design system
2	
3	The contract for the customer-facing portal (`app/(portal)/**`) and the builder
4	(`app/projects/[id]/**`). Marketing pages (`app/page.tsx`, `/pricing`, `/blog`,
5	`/templates`, `/wizard`) are a **separate** system — do not repoint their tokens.
6	
7	## The one-sentence brief
8	
9	An AI website builder that happens to have a customer portal around it — not a
10	dashboard that happens to contain a builder. The primary action is always
11	"build something".
12	
13	---
14	
15	## Tokens
16	
17	Defined in `app/globals.css`, exposed to Tailwind via `@theme inline`. **Use the
18	Tailwind class, never a raw hex and never an arbitrary-value bracket.**
19	
20	### Surface
21	
22	| Class | Use |
23	| --- | --- |
24	| `bg-canvas` | The page behind panels. Set by `AppShell`; pages never set it. |
25	| `bg-surface` | Cards, panels, the sidebar. |
26	| `bg-surface-2` | Hover, inset rows, quiet fills. |
27	| `bg-surface-3` | Track of a progress bar, the deepest step. |
28	| `bg-inset` | Code/preview wells. |
29	
30	### Line
31	
32	`border-hair` (default for cards) · `border-line-mid` (inputs, menus) ·
33	`border-line-strong` (emphasis, pending step outline)
34	
35	### Text
36	
37	`text-ink` (primary) · `text-ink-2` (secondary/body) · `text-ink-3` (tertiary,
38	placeholder, disabled) · `text-ink-inv` (on a brand fill)
39	
40	### Brand
41	
42	`text-brand` `bg-brand` `bg-brand-tint` `bg-brand-tint-2` `text-brand-ink`
43	
44	`--brand-gradient` is a **fill of last resort**. Exactly one element per view may
45	carry it: the primary button. Do not gradient headings, cards, borders or icons.
46	
47	### Status
48	
49	`ok` `warn` `danger` `info`, each with a `-tint` companion
50	(`text-ok` / `bg-ok-tint`). Status colour is never the brand colour.
51	
52	### Radius / elevation / motion
53	
54	`rounded-sm|md|lg|xl|2xl` (8/10/14/20/28px) · `shadow-e1|e2|e3` ·
55	`duration-[var(--t-1)]` 120ms, `--t-2` 200ms, `--t-3` 380ms ·
56	`ease-[var(--ease)]`
57	
58	---
59	
60	## Utility classes
61	
62	`k-focus` — **put this on every interactive element.** One focus ring, product-wide.
63	`k-display` `k-h1` `k-h2` `k-label` — the type scale. `k-label` is the only uppercase.
64	`k-num` — **required** on any figure: credits, prices, counts, dates in a column.
65	`k-scroll-x` — wrap any wide table/code block. The page body must never scroll sideways.
66	`k-msg-in` `k-step-in` `k-step-active` — entrance and progress animations.
67	`k-preview-busy` / `k-preview-idle` — the preview treatment while the AI works.
68	`k-wash` — ambient brand glow inside a hero panel. Sparingly: one per page, at most.
69	`k-gradient-border` — gradient hairline. Reserve for the single most important panel.
70	
71	---
72	
73	## Components (`components/ui/`)
74	
75	Import these. **Do not hand-roll a second version of any of them.**
76	
77	| Component | Notes |
78	| --- | --- |
79	| `Button` `ButtonLink` `IconButton` `buttonClass` | Variants `primary\|secondary\|ghost\|soft\|danger`, sizes `xs\|sm\|md\|lg`. **One `primary` per view.** `IconButton` requires `label`. |
80	| `Card` `CardHeader` `SectionHeader` | `interactive` only if it truly responds. |
81	| `Badge` | `tone` + `dot` + `pulse`. Set `dot` on anything conveying live state — colour alone is not a status channel. |
82	| `Input` `Textarea` `Select` `SearchInput` | Label/hint/error/aria wiring is built in. Never hand-write a bare `<input>`. |
83	| `Progress` `toneForUsage` | Recolours as it fills. `indeterminate` for work with no known end. |
84	| `Skeleton` `SkeletonList` | Stagger with `delay`. |
85	| `EmptyState` | `kind` is required: `empty` (none yet) / `no-results` (filter too narrow) / `unavailable` (does not exist yet). These need different sentences. |
86	| `Menu` | Keyboard + Escape + click-outside already handled. `unavailableReason` greys an item and says why. |
87	| `Modal` `ConfirmModal` | Native `<dialog>`. Confirm buttons are labelled with the verb, never "OK". |
88	| `ToastProvider` `useToast` | Provider is already mounted by `AppShell`. Errors and toasts with an action do not auto-dismiss. |
89	| `Segmented` | Real radios. Used for grid/list and device toggles. |
90	| `AIProgress` `stepsAt` | **The** progress component. See below. |
91	| `Stat` `StatRow` | Any number the customer must understand. |
92	| `Avatar` | Initials only — there is no avatar upload. |
93	| `Spinner` | |
94	
95	## Shell (`components/app/`)
96	
97	`AppShell` wraps every portal page and already provides the sidebar, mobile
98	drawer, bottom bar and toast host. **A page renders content only** — no page
99	supplies its own nav, no page sets a background, no page mounts a second
100	`ToastProvider`.
101	
102	Navigation lives in `components/app/nav.ts`. An item may only be added there
103	once it is backed by real data; `soon: true` marks the ones that are not.
104	
105	---
106	
107	## AI progress is one object, not three spinners
108	
109	`AIProgress` is rendered by the initial build overlay, by the chat panel during
110	an edit, and beside the preview. All three must show the **same steps in the
111	same state**, because the customer reads them as one thing happening.
112	
113	**Drive `state` from real build signals.** A timer that walks the list forward on
114	its own is a fake — and it will still be sitting on "Finalizing" long after a
115	build has failed. The build genuinely does not know its percentage (it is an
116	agent loop of unknown length), which is exactly why this is a named-step list
117	and not a progress bar.
118	
119	---
120	
121	## What does not exist (audited — do not build UI that pretends otherwise)
122	
123	| Thing | Reality |
124	| --- | --- |
125	| **Plans / subscriptions** | None. No plan, price, or renewal date. Checkout is one-off `payment` mode for credit packs. **Never render a "Pro" chip or "$X/month".** |
126	| **Credit reset date** | Credits never expire. There is no monthly allowance and no reset day — the spend cap is a *rolling* 30 days chosen so there is no reset. |
127	| **Invoices / payment method** | Not fetched from Stripe. The credit ledger is the only history. |
128	| **Thumbnails** | Nothing captures a screenshot. No headless browser. |
129	| **Project status** | Only `publishedAt` → Published / Draft. No `archived`. "Building" is derivable from `Build.status = RUNNING` but has no staleness rule, so it is not yet trustworthy. |
130	| **Domains** | No model, no field, no route. Sites live at `<slug>.kodely.site` only. |
131	| **Integrations** | Nothing customer-facing. |
132	| **Support tickets** | No ticket model. `SupportNote` is admin-write-only and explicitly never shown to the customer. |
133	| **Storage / bandwidth** | Not measured anywhere. |
134	| **Workspaces / members / roles** | No concept of it. Ownership is one FK: `Project.userId`. |
135	| **Avatar upload, password change, 2FA, notification prefs** | None. |
136	
137	**Sessions list and revoke, and editing `User.name`, ARE cheaply real** — the
138	`Session` model is per-user and queryable.
139	
140	### The rule
141	
142	A screen that looks operable and is not is worse than an absent one. A screen
143	that says "this does not exist yet, here is what you have instead" is neither.
144	Use `EmptyState kind="unavailable"` and say plainly what is missing.

1	// Kodely — Phase 1 data model.
2	// Principles baked in here (see the Kodely board):
3	//  - every generation is a Build row with real token counts, so cost per build is never a guess
4	//  - credits are a ledger, never a mutable counter: the balance is derivable and auditable
5	//  - failed builds are recorded but NEVER charged
6	
7	generator client {
8	  provider = "prisma-client-js"
9	}
10	
11	datasource db {
12	  provider = "postgresql"
13	  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
14	}
15	
16	model User {
17	  id               String   @id @default(cuid())
18	  email            String   @unique
19	  // Nullable because a Google-only account never sets a local password.
20	  passwordHash     String?
21	  googleId         String?  @unique
22	  name             String?
23	  role             String   @default("CUSTOMER") // CUSTOMER | ADMIN
24	  stripeCustomerId String?
25	  createdAt        DateTime @default(now())
26	
27	  // Self-imposed ceiling on credits spent per rolling 30 days. NULL = no cap.
28	  // This is the user's own guard against a runaway session, not a plan limit —
29	  // bill shock is the category's deepest trust wound (one competitor billed
30	  // $607 against a $25 plan in three days), and a cap the user sets themselves
31	  // is the cheapest honest answer to it.
32	  spendCapCredits Int?
33	
34	  // Set when the user asks for erasure, cleared if they cancel. The grace
35	  // period is measured from here.
36	  //
37	  // Exists because the alternative was worse: the request was being recorded as
38	  // marker-prefixed SupportNote rows, which then appeared in an operator-notes
39	  // UI that describes itself as "operator-written, never customer-facing" — one
40	  // of those rows was neither. A lifecycle fact belongs on the user, not
41	  // smuggled into a table meant for something else.
42	  deletionRequestedAt DateTime?
43	
44	  sessions     Session[]
45	  projects     Project[]
46	  ledger       CreditLedger[]
47	  events       Event[]
48	  supportNotes SupportNote[]
49	}
50	
51	// First-party analytics. Self-hosted deliberately: cheaper, keeps the data
52	// ours, avoids another paid API on the critical path, and is privacy-clean.
53	//
54	// One wide table rather than a table per dashboard, because the activation
55	// funnel, retention cohorts, per-user journey, attribution and the overview
56	// tiles are all different queries over the same stream. Build it once, or
57	// every dashboard invents its own tracking.
58	model Event {
59	  id     String  @id @default(cuid())
60	  // Nullable so pre-signup events (landing view, prompt submitted) still land.
61	  userId String?
62	  /// Dotted, past-tense name — see EVENTS in lib/events.ts. Never free text.
63	  name   String
64	  /// Small, non-PII payload: ids, counts, enum-ish strings. Never prompt bodies.
65	  props  Json?
66	
67	  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
68	
69	  user User? @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)
70	
71	  // Funnels scan by name over a window; journeys scan one user over a window.
72	  @@index([name, createdAt])
73	  @@index([userId, createdAt])
74	}
75	
76	// A submission from a form on a PUBLISHED generated site.
77	//
78	// This is the one deliberate hole in "generated sites have no backend", and it
79	// exists because the alternative is worse: the builder is currently forbidden
80	// from drawing a contact form at all, because a form that silently discards a
81	// real enquiry is worse than no form — and a live blog post already told dental
82	// practices their appointment requests were arriving when they were not.
83	//
84	// Submissions land HERE, on Kodely's origin, never on the customer's site. The
85	// generated page stays static; only the POST target is ours.
86	model FormSubmission {
87	  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
88	  projectId String
89	  /// Which form on the page, when a site has more than one.
90	  formName  String   @default("contact")
91	  /// The submitted fields. Untrusted public input — never rendered as HTML,
92	  /// never interpolated into a query, and capped hard at write time.
93	  fields    Json
94	  /// For rate limiting and abuse triage only. Not shown to the site owner.
95	  ipHash    String?
96	  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
97	
98	  readAt DateTime?
99	  /// Set when it looks like spam. Kept rather than dropped, so a false
100	  /// positive is recoverable and the rate is measurable.
101	  spam   Boolean @default(false)
102	
103	  project Project @relation(fields: [projectId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
104	
105	  @@index([projectId, createdAt])
106	  @@index([createdAt])
107	}
108	
109	// Pre-auth attempt counter for login and signup.
110	//
111	// Exists because the limiter that guards them cannot key on a user id — there
112	// is no session yet — and every other limiter in lib/rate-limit.ts counts rows
113	// the feature already writes (Build, Project). A failed login writes nothing,
114	// so without this table the counter can only live in process memory, where it
115	// resets on every deploy and multiplies by the process count.
116	//
117	// `key` is the bucket, already hashed by the caller: an IP, or a salted digest
118	// of an email. Deliberately never the plaintext address — this table would
119	// otherwise become a running list of every address anyone tried to log in as,
120	// which is a worse thing to hold than the problem it solves.
121	model LoginAttempt {
122	  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
123	  key       String
124	  /// "ip" | "account" | "signup" — so one table serves every pre-auth bucket
125	  /// without the scopes colliding on a shared key.
126	  scope     String
127	  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
128	
129	  // The only query shape: count rows for one bucket inside a window, and prune
130	  // everything older. Both are served by this index.
131	  @@index([scope, key, createdAt])
132	  @@index([createdAt])
133	}
134	
135	// One row per transactional email actually sent.
136	//
137	// Without this, notification idempotency has to be derived from a time window,
138	// which is at-most-once: a skipped cron run drops that window, and a process
139	// restart mid-window can resend. The unique constraint below makes it
140	// exactly-once — the insert IS the claim, so two workers racing produce one
141	// email and one conflict.
142	//
143	// `dedupeKey` is the id of the thing that triggered it (the ledger row that
144	// dropped someone into "low", the failed build, the project first published),
145	// NOT a timestamp. That is what makes the guarantee independent of scheduling.
146	model EmailLog {
147	  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
148	  userId    String
149	  /// welcome | low_credits | build_failed | site_published
150	  kind      String
151	  dedupeKey String
152	  sentAt    DateTime @default(now())
153	
154	  @@unique([kind, dedupeKey])
155	  @@index([userId, sentAt])
156	}
157	
158	// Who did what in the admin panel. Admin surfaces read cost, margin, customer
159	// prompts and personal data; without a log, "who looked at this account" has no
160	// answer. Append-only by convention — nothing in the app updates or deletes a row.
161	model AdminAuditLog {
162	  id         String   @id @default(cuid())
163	  /// The admin who acted. Kept as a plain id, not a relation, so the record
164	  /// survives that admin's account being deleted.
165	  actorId    String
166	  actorEmail String
167	  /// Dotted, past-tense: "user.viewed", "site.taken_down", "flag.changed".
168	  action     String
169	  targetType String?
170	  targetId   String?
171	  /// Small, non-PII context. Never prompt bodies or generated content.
172	  meta       Json?
173	  createdAt  DateTime @default(now())
174	
175	  @@index([actorId, createdAt])
176	  @@index([action, createdAt])
177	  @@index([targetType, targetId])
178	}
179	
180	// Runtime kill switches and gradual rollout. Deliberately a table rather than
181	// env vars: flipping a flag must not require a deploy, which is the entire
182	// point of having a kill switch.
183	model FeatureFlag {
184	  key         String   @id
185	  enabled     Boolean  @default(false)
186	  description String   @default("")
187	  /// 0-100. Ignored when `enabled` is false. Bucketed by user id so a given
188	  /// user's answer is stable rather than flickering between requests.
189	  rolloutPct  Int      @default(100)
190	  updatedAt   DateTime @updatedAt
191	  updatedBy   String?
192	}
193	
194	// One row per moderation finding per publish attempt. Sub-blocking findings
195	// previously went only to console.warn — enough to reconstruct one site after
196	// it is reported, not enough to query proactively, and not enough to ever
197	// measure the false-positive rate that gates promoting a rule to blocking.
198	model ModerationFinding {
199	  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
200	  projectId String
201	  rule      String
202	  severity  String // high | medium | low
203	  path      String
204	  evidence  String
205	  /// "blocked" when this finding stopped the publish, "recorded" otherwise.
206	  action    String
207	  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
208	
209	  reviewedAt DateTime?
210	  reviewedBy String?
211	  /// Set on review: "true_positive" | "false_positive".
212	  outcome    String?
213	
214	  @@index([projectId, createdAt])
215	  @@index([severity, createdAt])
216	  @@index([rule, createdAt])
217	}
218	
219	// Operator-written notes about a customer, for support continuity. Never shown
220	// to the customer, so it must never be used to store anything we would not
221	// stand behind if disclosed in a data-subject access request.
222	model SupportNote {
223	  id          String   @id @default(cuid())
224	  userId      String
225	  authorEmail String
226	  body        String
227	  createdAt   DateTime @default(now())
228	
229	  user User @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
230	
231	  @@index([userId, createdAt])
232	}
233	
234	// Every processed Stripe webhook event, keyed by Stripe's own event id.
235	// This is the idempotency guard: a webhook retry (Stripe resends on any
236	// non-2xx or timeout) must never grant credits twice for the same payment.
237	model StripeEvent {
238	  id        String   @id
239	  type      String
240	  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
241	}
242	
243	model Session {
244	  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
245	  userId    String
246	  tokenHash String   @unique
247	  expiresAt DateTime
248	  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
249	
250	  user User @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
251	
252	  @@index([userId])
253	}
254	
255	model Project {
256	  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
257	  userId    String
258	  name      String
259	  slug      String   @unique // becomes <slug>.kodely.site when published
260	  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
261	  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt
262	
263	  publishedAt DateTime?
264	
265	  user     User          @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
266	  files       ProjectFile[]

content.text:
## What I built

**`/dashboard` — home** (`app/(portal)/dashboard/page.tsx`, server component)
- `k-wash` hero (one per page): "Welcome back, \<name\>", the single `primary` button **Create Website → /dashboard/new**, a secondary **New site** (the real, working blank-project path), and three inline figures — sites / published / credits.
- `FirstRunChecklist` kept intact, just repositioned. I deliberately did **not** edit `FirstRunPanel`, and I labelled `NewProjectButton` "New site" because that panel's copy tells people to look for that exact wording.
- **Needs-attention strip** (renders only when something is actually true): out of credits, balance below your own average build cost, spend cap reached, a build that failed in the last 7 days.
- **Websites overview** — 3 most-recent `WebsiteCard`s + "View all".
- **Credits** — remaining, "about N more builds" from `averageBuildCredits()`, your own average as a second stat, and the rolling-30-day spend cap as a real `Progress` bar (it has a genuine max; credits do not, so there is no credit bar and no reset date anywhere).
- **Recent activity** — `Event` over `@@index([userId, createdAt])`, filtered to the five customer-meaningful names.
- **Quick actions** → `/dashboard/templates`, `/dashboard/billing`, `/settings`.

**`/dashboard/websites`** — `page.tsx` (server), `WebsitesBrowser.tsx` (client), `data.ts` (shared loader/formatters). Grid+list via `Segmented`, search over name and slug, sort by updated/created/name, status filter. State is client-side over the already-loaded list, mirrored into the URL with `history.replaceState` so a filtered view is shareable without re-querying Postgres per keystroke; the server seeds initial state from `searchParams`.

**`components/app/WebsiteCard.tsx`** — one component for both grid and list, so the two views cannot disagree. Menu actions all hit real routes: Open live site, Edit, Rename (`Modal` + `Input`), Duplicate, Publish/Republish, Delete (`ConfirmModal`).

## What I found that was not real

- **`/dashboard/new`, `/dashboard/templates`, `/support` did not exist when I started** — parallel agents created them mid-task. All my links now resolve on disk.
- **`Event.props` has no project name.** Names are joined per render; `project.deleted` renders "Deleted a site" (there is nothing left to join to) and a stale reference renders "a site that's no longer here". No raw id is ever printed.
- **Publish 400s when there is no compiled draft tree.** I now precompute that and grey the action with `unavailableReason: "Nothing built yet"` rather than letting it fail.
- **`window.prompt()`** in `NewProjectButton` — replaced with a `Modal` + `Input`. It was also silently a no-op in browsers that block prompts.

## What I deliberately did not build

- **No Archived filter.** No soft-delete column exists. Archive stays *visible* in the menu with `unavailableReason: "Doesn't exist yet"`, because people go looking for it.
- **Building is offered, with a stated rule.** A site reads as Building only while a `RUNNING` build is younger than **10 minutes** — double the `maxDuration = 300` ceiling the generate route itself enforces, so an abandoned SSE row collapses instead of claiming to build forever. The rule is stated in the page footnote and in the "no results" copy.
- **No credit progress bar** — there is no allowance to be a fraction of.
- **`ProjectRow.tsx` / `SignOutButton.tsx`**: the sandbox blocked file deletion. `ProjectRow` is now a re-export shim pointing at `WebsiteCard` (its hand-rolled menu/modal/focus-ring duplicates are gone); `SignOutButton` is restyled onto the design system but is no longer rendered — `AppShell`'s `UserMenu` already owns sign-out. **Both should just be deleted.**

## Thumbnail decision

A **generated cover**, never a screenshot and deliberately not shaped like one — no browser chrome, no fake page layout. It is a gradient field with a fine dot pattern and the site's monogram, rendered as inline SVG.

- If the project has a **brand kit** (`ProjectFile` kind `"brand"` / `brand.json`, via `parseStoredBrandKit`), the gradient is the site's **real** `palette.primary → secondary`.
- Otherwise it is a deterministic FNV-1a hash of the slug into eight curated pairs — stable forever, distinct between neighbours.

Stated in plain language in the page header and again in the footnote: *"Covers are generated from each site's own colours — Kodely doesn't capture screenshots."*

## Tradeoff you should know about

The old `ProjectRow` required **typing the site's exact name** to delete a published site. `ConfirmModal` has no typed-confirmation affordance, and the brief mandates `ConfirmModal`, so that gate is gone — replaced by an explicit two-step whose body states that the live address goes offline immediately and cannot be reclaimed. If you want the typed gate back, `ConfirmModal` needs a `requireText` prop rather than a second bespoke dialog.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit`: **zero errors in my files.** (Pre-existing errors remain in `app/projects/[id]/Editor.tsx` and stale `.next/dev/types` — another agent's in-flight work, not mine.)
- `npx eslint` on all nine owned paths with `--max-warnings=0`: **clean.** `react-hooks/purity` caught `Date.now()` in the page body; fixed properly by moving the clock read into `daysAgo()` in `data.ts` rather than suppressing it.
- Both routes compile and return 307 to login on the running dev server, including with hostile params (`?view=constructor&sort=__proto__&status=toString`).

**Untested:** I could not sign in (creating accounts and entering passwords is off-limits to me), so **no signed-in state has been rendered.** Everything past the auth redirect — actual card layout, the grid/list toggle, search/sort/filter behaviour, the rename/duplicate/publish/delete round-trips, toasts, the activity join, and both empty states — is verified by types and reading only, not by looking at it. Responsive behaviour is likewise unverified visually.
